in_text_mentions: on three key anatomical features: the relationship of the great arteries, the presence of a VSD, and the degree of pulmonary obstruction. Type I (69%) is characterized by normal anatomy of the great arteries (Figure 3). Type II (28%) involves D-transposition of the great arteries (D-TGA) (Figure 4). Type III (3%) involves great artery positions other than D-transposition. Type IV encompasses malposition defects, such as truncus arteriosus [17]. CT angiography can evaluate TV morphology and display the relationship between the heart and great vessels, making it valuable for clinical management.
